t: This Gothic Revival tower stands at the corner of Westminster Bridge Road and Kennington Road. It is the Lincoln Memorial Tower, opened in 1876 in memory of Abraham Lincoln and paid for partly by Americans. Lincoln was the sixteenth American president, who led his country through the Civil War and played a major role in abolishing slavery. The tower is all that remains of a nineteenth-century complex of philanthropic institutions beside a Congregational chapel. Today it houses small meeting rooms and is a listed building, close to Christ Church and Upton Chapel.
